title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR Denique — Pontificii / Bellarmine / Chamier
pass_a_gloss: GAR. Finally the Pontiffs use a like argument, in order to prove that those words, this is my body, are not to be understood figuratively, because a pact, a sacrament, a law, require a proper not a figured locution: for so Bellarmine and Costerus. Our men answering deny it, as is to be seen in Chamier book 10 on the Eucharist, chapter 15, numbers 60, 61.
pass_b_english: GAR. Finally the Papists use a like argument to prove that the words 'this is my body' must not be taken figuratively, because a covenant, a sacrament, and a law require proper—not figurative—speech: so Bellarmine and Coster. Our writers deny it in reply, as you may see in Chamier, book 10 on the Eucharist, chapter 15, §§60–61.
source_text: GAR. Denique pari argumento utuntur Pontificii, ut probent illa verba, hoc est corpus meum, non esse intelligenda figurate, quia pactum, sacramentum, lex, requirunt propriam non figuratam locutionem: ita enim Bellarminus & Costerus. Nostri respondentes negant, ut videre est apud Chamierum lib. 10. de Eucharist. cap. 15. n. 60. 61.

choices.choice: Pontificii eucharist parity via Bellarmine/Coster; Chamier reply cited
